why: Holmes states the bell-rope is fastened to a hook just above where the ventilator opening is.
The ventilator is named in the same passage ('the little opening for the ventilator').

text: The wire a bell-rope would be attached to
why: Holmes says the rope 'is not even attached to a wire'.

text: That afternoon: Holmes shows that the rope is fastened to a hook above the ventilator
why: The scene takes place in the afternoon (Holmes greets Miss Stoner with 'Good-afternoon'), and the hook is shown at this point.

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — to give a reason for having a hook at that spot
id: q.why_bell_rope=to give a reason for having a hook at that spot
why: Holmes has just said the bell-pull seemed unnecessary and was recently installed, and the hook sits at the ventilator, so a reader has reason to consider this as a possible purpose.

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — it is a dummy, not even attached to a wire
why: Holmes says 'it's a dummy' and that it is not attached to a wire.

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — it runs from just above the opening of the ventilator down to the pillow
why: The rope is fastened to a hook just above the ventilator opening, and its tassel lies on the pillow, so it runs from there down to the pillow.
